I’ll also request two-speaker labeling and leave deletion to your retention job.

```python
import assemblyai as aai

aai.settings.api_key = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"

# audio_file = "./local_file.mp3"
audio_file = "https://assembly.ai/wildfires.mp3"

config = aai.TranscriptionConfig(
    speech_models=["universal-3-5-pro", "universal-2"],
    language_detection=True,
).set_redact_pii(
    policies=[
        aai.PIIRedactionPolicy.person_name,
        aai.PIIRedactionPolicy.organization,
        aai.PIIRedactionPolicy.occupation,
    ],
    substitution=aai.PIISubstitutionPolicy.hash,
)

transcript = aai.Transcriber().transcribe(audio_file, config)
print(f"Transcript ID:", transcript.id)

print(transcript.text)
```

Once the `Transcript` object is returned, you can access the URL of the redacted audio file with `get_redacted_audio_url`, or save the redacted audio directly to disk with `save_redacted_audio`.

Implemented [run.sh](/work/run.sh). No installation needed.

```sh
./run.sh <audio.wav> <out.json>
```

It requests two-speaker labeling and server-side redaction of names, SSNs, and phone numbers, writes the required JSON, and exits nonzero on failure. It never deletes transcripts.

Tested successfully with `sample.wav`; verified AssemblyAI’s retained result matches the redacted output.

Speakers use labels A/B. Automated PII detection can miss sensitive information, so it cannot guarantee an absolute no-PII result.
